requirement_text.REQ-064: Execute Decision 0006's D2: drop tenant_id from ten schema-isolated business tables. Full acceptance criteria: see handoffs/WF02-REQ064-20260818/step-03-test-designer.json's requirement_text.

task.description:
TEST-DESIGNER's own run took several dispatches to complete due to unrelated infrastructure interruptions (a nested background process hit a transient API error) -- the work itself, once it finished, was independently re-verified: ORCH ran the full suite twice directly (775/775 both times) and TEST-DESIGNER's own final report separately confirms 775/775 across two of its own runs, with one flaky failure in test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs's :auto-mode DropLegacyPublicIdentityTables guard test isolated and attributed to pre-existing connection-pool-timing flakiness (REQ-063-era code, untouched by this requirement), not a REQ-064 regression. Confirm this attribution yourself -- read that specific test, check whether this diff touched anything it depends on (it shouldn't have, per the design's own scope boundary), and if you also hit this flake, re-run just that file in isolation 3-4 times to confirm it's genuinely intermittent and not deterministic under some condition this diff introduced.

Read test/specs/REQ-064.md and the actual test source directly -- do not read TEST-DESIGNER's handoff result.summary as a substitute.

TEST-DESIGNER found and fixed a genuine production bug beyond pure test work: lib/letflow/identity_migration.ex's copy_groups/2, copy_users/2, copy_tenant_roles/2 used fragment("? = ?", g.tenant_id, ^tenant_id) which relied on the now-removed Group/User Ecto field declaration for UUID type inference -- once that field was dropped, Postgrex received a raw UUID string instead of the 16-byte binary form, causing a real DBConnection.EncodeError. Fixed with explicit type(^tenant_id, Ecto.UUID) casts. Verify this fix is correct and complete: read all three call sites directly, confirm the type/2 cast is present and correctly typed, and confirm this was a genuine pre-existing-but-latent bug this same PR's own column drop exposed (not something the fix itself introduces or masks).

Several tests were restructured (not just patched) because their entire purpose was proving something about the now-removed tenant_id field -- event_store_test.exs's AC6 block, promotion_review_store_test.exs's prefix-derivation block, store_test.exs's AC9 block, engine/schemas_test.exs's moduledoc-content test. For each, confirm the restructured version still proves the SAME underlying acceptance-criterion claim (typically via schema-prefix reachability instead of a direct field read), not a weaker or different claim.

Standard procedure: for each REQ-064 acceptance criterion, verify at least one runnable test targets it, no TODO-implement-test deferrals, tests self-sufficient and don't depend on execution order, no hardcoded secrets/connection strings, per-test unique fixture data.
acceptance_criteria: Every REQ-064 acceptance criterion has at least one runnable test, verified against actual test source
The identity_migration_test.exs flake independently confirmed pre-existing/unrelated, not a REQ-064 regression
identity_migration.ex's type(^tenant_id, Ecto.UUID) fix verified correct at all three call sites

Each restructured test (event_store_test.exs, promotion_review_store_test.exs, store_test.exs, engine/schemas_test.exs) confirmed to still prove its original acceptance-criterion claim, not a weaker one
Test fixtures use per-test unique data, no shared hardcoded tenant/schema names
